The SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) (Amendment) Regulations, 2021 (w.e.f. 03-08-2021) substituted the definition of 'credit rating agency' under Regulation 2(h). The original definition restricted 'credit rating agencies' to entities rating securities 'offered by way of public or rights issue' — covering only primary market issuances. The 2021 amendment broadened the definition to cover rating of securities 'that are listed or proposed to be listed on a stock exchange recognized by the Board' — expanding the scope to include all listed securities and not just those offered via public or rights issues.

The promoter must maintain at least 26% shareholding for a minimum of three years from the date of grant of registration. Three years from April 1, 2023 = April 1, 2026. June 15, 2026 is after April 1, 2026, so the lock-in period of three years has expired by then. After April 1, 2026, the promoter is no longer bound by the 3-year lock-in. However, reducing to 20% would breach the minimum 26% threshold if this obligation is ongoing beyond the three-year period (which the regulation's wording 'for a minimum period of three years' suggests is a lock-in, not a permanent requirement). The regulation specifies a minimum period of three years; after that, the 26% floor from Regulation 9(e) no longer applies as a mandatory minimum. Therefore, the promoter can reduce its shareholding to 20% on June 15, 2026.
